newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK securities body proposes OTC reporting regime.
newsitem.headline: HK securities body proposes OTC reporting regime.

text.p: Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) said on Friday it was proposing that firms inform it of over-the-counter (OTC) derivatives activities rather than comply with an international regime.
The SFC said it had decided that general imposition of an International Organisation of Securities Commissions and Basle Committee reporting framework was not warranted in Hong Kong.
"Two successive surveys indicated the overwhelming majority of the firms registered with the SFC were not involved in OTC derivatives activities," it said in a statement.
"Instead a general reporting requirement on the fact of OTC derivatives activities to alert the SFC of the need to monitor a registered intermediary's activities is proposed."
A more detailed reporting requirement would be introduced once a firm had alerted the SFC, it said.
The proposed reporting regime "would not be intrusive, cumbersome or costly to implement and is appropriate for Hong Kong circumstances", the SFC said.
